comment: No sql: permissions — all SQL lives in Rust behind typed commands (ADR-0002). The plugin is present only for its migration runner. dialog:allow-save opens the native Save as… box for the xlsx export and dialog:allow-open picks the backup folder; both return a path, not a file handle — Rust writes the bytes. No autostart: permissions either: the checkbox goes through update_settings so the registry and the settings row are written together. updater:default lets the frontend ask whether there is a newer TimeBuddy and install it; process:allow-restart is the relaunch that finishes that, and is deliberately the only process: permission — process:allow-exit would be a second way out of the app, and the way out is the tray's Quit (ADR-0004).
